Failures are caught, so the route still answers even when services are down, which is useful but should be tested.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and setup
sections.what: Brings in the route tools, the public marker, the database access and the cache service.
sections.why: Needed to run the database and cache checks.

sections.name: HealthController (part 1)
sections.title: Checking database and cache
sections.what: Runs a test query on the database and counts users, then writes and reads a short test key in Redis. Each check records whether it worked and how long it took.
sections.why: Likely reason: confirms the two services the API cannot run without.
sections.watch_out: The check writes a test key to Redis every time, so frequent polling adds small load.

sections.name: HealthController (part 2)
sections.title: Building the health response
sections.what: Combines the two checks into one answer. It says healthy only when both pass, otherwise degraded, and includes uptime, total time and details for each service.
sections.why: Gives monitoring tools one simple answer plus details for debugging.
sections.watch_out: The response contains detailed error text and the total user count, which should be reviewed before exposing this route publicly.

summary: Provides a public health check that reports whether the database and Redis cache are reachable.
purpose: Lets hosting tools and operators see whether the API and its main dependencies are working.
why: Likely reason: monitoring systems need a simple endpoint to decide if the service is healthy.
how: Runs a trivial database query and counts users, then writes and reads a test value in Redis. It measures the time each check takes and returns overall healthy or degraded with details.
inputs: No inputs. The route is open to anyone.
outputs: A status object with overall status, time, uptime, latency and details for the database and Redis.
risks: The route is public and reports the number of users and raw error messages, which can reveal internal details to anyone.
debug: If the status is degraded, read the database and redis fields for the error text. A slow response points to database or cache latency.
